item.title: The Peacock Throne: The Shah Who Emptied Delhi
item.description:
Tells how the Persian ruler Nadir Shah scattered the Mughal army at Karnal in seventeen thirty-nine in a matter of hours, then entered Delhi, sacked the city, and carried off a treasure that included the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor. The episode covers how that single campaign turned the Mughal Empire into a hollow shell and opened India to new masters.
Konular: nadir shah, mughal empire, battle of karnal, peacock throne, koh-i-noor.

item.title: Talas 751: The Captives Who Carried Paper West
item.description:
Tells of the single encounter between Tang China and the newly founded Abbasid Caliphate on the banks of the Talas River, on today's Kyrgyzstan–Kazakhstan border, in July seven hundred and fifty-one, and how the Tang army fell apart when the Karluks changed sides in the middle of the fight. The episode follows the Chinese artisans taken captive to trace how papermaking travelled to Samarkand and Baghdad, asks how much of that account is true, and covers the Tang withdrawal from Central Asia.
Konular: battle of talas, tang dynasty, abbasids, karluks, history of paper.

item.title: The Winter War: Soviet Divisions Swallowed by the Snow
item.description:
Recounts the Soviet Union's attack on Finland on the thirtieth of November, nineteen thirty-nine, and the resistance put up for one hundred and five days by a country fifty times smaller in population. The episode ranges from the Soviet divisions torn apart in the snow at Suomussalmi and on the Raate Road to the Moscow Peace, and to the way the weakness displayed by the Red Army emboldened Hitler toward Barbarossa.
Konular: winter war, finland, soviet union, motti tactic, mannerheim line.

item.title: The Ten Thousand: An Army Stranded Inside Persia
item.description:
Tells how the more than ten thousand Greek mercenaries hired by Cyrus the Younger to take the Persian throne from his brother in four hundred and one BC were left leaderless and friendless in the very heart of the empire when Cyrus died at Cunaxa, and how they marched fifteen hundred miles back to the Black Sea. The episode ranges from the ambush and killing of the generals at a banquet to Xenophon's election to command, from the winter crossing of the Anatolian mountains to the way this march exposed Persian weakness to the Greek world.
Konular: ancient greece, persian empire, xenophon, ten thousand, mercenaries.
